hints: Look at where the ester splits apart, the C=O side comes from the acid and the O-alkyl side comes from the alcohol.
Count the carbons on the left of the C=O group, there are three carbons plus the carbonyl carbon itself to name the acid.
Look at the group on the right of the single O, it has three carbons with the O attached to the middle carbon, so think which propanol isomer that must be.
walkthrough:
**Split the ester into its two parents**

Think of ester formation as a jigsaw. The acid provides the acyl part, the alcohol provides the alkyl part.

General equation:
$$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify the carboxylic acid from the left side**

Look left of the $\text{C=O}$. Ester Z has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C=O}$, that is a 4-carbon chain including the carbonyl carbon.

That parent acid is:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$ which is butanoic acid.

**Identify the alcohol from the right side**

Look right of the single $\text{-O-}$. Ester Z has $\text{-O-CH(CH}_3\text{)}_2$, a 3-carbon group joined through the middle carbon.

That parent alcohol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, which is propan-2-ol. Together, butanoic acid + propan-2-ol give the correct ester.

options.A: Incorrect. Butan-1-ol would give a straight 4-carbon O-alkyl group, $\text{-OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, not the branched 3-carbon group seen. Also 'methyl propanoic acid' is not the correct name for the 4-carbon acid part.
options.B: Incorrect. The acid is right (butanoic acid) but the alcohol is wrong. Propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, would give a straight chain $\text{-OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ ester, not the branched $\text{-OCH(CH}_3\text{)}_2$ shown.
options.C: Correct. Butanoic acid supplies the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO-}$ part and propan-2-ol supplies the $\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)}_2$ part. Condensation with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives exactly ester Z, propan-2-yl butanoate.
options.D: Incorrect. The alcohol is right (propan-2-ol) but the acid is too short. Propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, has only 3 carbons and would give a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO-}$ left side, but Z clearly has one more $\text{CH}_2$ group.
